stem: The immediate cause of the Deccan Riots of 1875 was:

options.label: b
options.text: High interest rates charged by Mahajans

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above above/More than one of the above

expl: The Deccan Riots of 1875 had many causes, such as: high interest rates charged by Mahajans and peasants becoming permanently indebted; high interest rates related to land revenue; getting peasants to sign loan documents by mortgaging their fields, houses, etc., due to illiteracy and poverty; and the failure of peasants to protect their interests due to the complex and costly judicial system. The Bihar Public Service Commission considered option (b) as the correct answer.

expl: In 1921–22, the peasants of Awadh ran a movement known as the Eka Movement. This movement was concentrated in the Hardoi, Bahraich, Barabanki, and Sitapur regions. The chief leader of the Eka Movement was Madari Pasi.

stem: What was the aim of Eka Movement in Oudh?

options.label: a
options.text: To stop to giving rent to the Government

options.label: b
options.text: To protect the rights of landlords

expl: The Eka Movement (1921–22) was led by Madari Pasi. The main centres of this movement were Hardoi, Barabanki, Bahraich and Sitapur. The peasants main complaints were the increase in land revenue and the practice of collecting land revenue in the form of produce. More than 50% land revenue was being taken from the peasants. The zamindars’ agents (thekedars) used to harass the peasants. The Eka Movement had little faith in the non-violent policies laid down by the nationalists. As a result, the nationalist leaders became separated from the movement, and the movement took a different path. In this movement, paying land revenue to the government was not stopped; rather, the main demand of the agitators was—“Due to rising inflation, land revenue should be converted into cash payment.”

stem: Who was associated with the Kisan Movement in Bihar?
expl: Rajendra Prasad was associated with the peasant movement in Bihar. He was associated with Mahatma Gandhi in Bihar during the Champaran Satyagraha (1917). He was the Food and Agriculture Minister in the Interim Government formed in September 1946 and was also the President of the Constituent Assembly. After the Constitution came into force, he became the first President of India.

stem: Who presided over the first session of All India Kisan Sabha?
expl: In April 1936, in Lucknow, the ‘All India Kisan Congress’ was formed, which was later renamed the ‘All India Kisan Sabha’. stem: Swami Sahajananda Saraswati formed the All India United Kisan Sabha with the demand for the ‘nationalisation of land and waterways’ :
expl: The All India Kisan Sabha was formed in 1936. Swami Sahajanand Saraswati was elected its first President and N.G. Ranga its General Secretary. In 1949 (shortly before his death), Sahajanand formed the All India United Kisan Sabha. The basic demand of this organisation was the nationalisation of land, waterways, energy, and all sources of wealth and property.

stem: The Sarabandi Campaign of 1922 was led by

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: After 1928, Bardoli (in Surat district of Gujarat) became a centre of political activities. The ‘Mehta brothers’ of Bardoli (Kalyanji and Kunvarji) and Dayalji Desai started an agitation in support of the peasants from 1928. Later, it was led by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel. Under Patel’s leadership, the ‘No-Tax (Sarabandi)’ movement was launched in 1928. It is noteworthy that during the Non-Cooperation Movement, Gandhiji had planned to launch a no-tax (Sarabandi) movement from Bardoli in 1922, but due to the Chauri-Chaura incident, this plan was postponed. The Bihar Public Service Commission has mistakenly written the year of the Sarabandi (no-tax) movement as 1922 instead of 1928, which is incorrect.

stem: When was All India Trade Union Congress established in Bombay?
expl: Through the efforts of N.M. Joshi, Joseph Baptista, and Lala Lajpat Rai, the “All India Trade Union Congress”, i.e., the All India Trade Union Congress (AITUC), was established in Bombay on 31 October, 1920. Lala Lajpat Rai was its first President, while Joseph Baptista was the Vice-President and Diwan Chamanlal Bajaj was the General Secretary. The first split in this organisation took place in 1929 at the Nagpur session. At that time, Jawaharlal Nehru was its President.

stem: The Revolutionary phase of the trade union movement in India was :
expl: The revolutionary phase of the trade union movement is considered to be from 1926 to 1939. During this period, M.N. Roy, Muzaffar Ahmad, Shripad A. Dange, Shaukat Usmani, etc. were the major leaders of the trade union movement in India.

stem: Identify the years closest to the establishment of the Communist Party of India and the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh respectively.
expl: The Communist Party of India and the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh were founded in 1925 at Kanpur and Nagpur, respectively.

stem: Who was the first Indian to be the member of Communist International?
expl: The Communist International (Comintern), also known as the Third International, was established in March, 1919 in Moscow. Vladimir Lenin (Vladimir Ilyich Ulyanov) and the Russian Communist Party (Bolshevik) played a major role in the formation of the Comintern. M.N. Roy went to Moscow on Lenin’s invitation and became a member of the Communist International. He was the first Indian to become a member of the Communist International.
